title: GitHub Trending Summary - Monthly - 2026-09-30
ranking_basis: Inferred monthly ranking from GitHub Search: current stars among repositories created this month, with recent push activity used as a freshness signal; no monthly star gains available.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: September’s standout signal is a fast-rising family of typed-decision models and tools built around Laya/Jev, appearing in model runtimes, coding-agent context management, and a phone assistant. A non-software evidence-based life guide also amassed a comparable star count, while new coding and design tools round out the month’s breakouts.

sections.title: eternity4719/HowToLiveBetter
sections.description: Evidence-based Chinese-language practical life guide covering health, finance, law, work, and family topics.
sections.content: An evidence-based Chinese-language practical life guide covering health, finance, law, work, and family topics. It led the month-created search results by current stars and was still being updated on September 30; it is a knowledge resource rather than a conventional software tool.

sections.title: NandhaKishorM/laya
sections.description: A multilingual, non-autoregressive decision engine for typed choices, scores, and yes/no decisions.
sections.content: A multilingual, non-autoregressive decision engine for typed choices, scores, and yes/no decisions. Its unusually high current star count in under two weeks, alongside active pushes through September 29, makes it the clearest model/research breakout.

sections.title: browser-use/jev-ultrafast
sections.description: A web-agent project focused on speed and low cost.
sections.content: A web-agent project focused on speed and low cost. It connects the emerging Jev decision-model interest to browser automation and was updated on September 30.

sections.title: lnkiai/m3e-canvas
sections.description: A browser-based tool for sketching Material 3 Expressive screens and generating prompts for AI-assisted coding.
sections.content: A browser-based tool for sketching Material 3 Expressive screens and generating prompts for AI-assisted coding. It is one of the month’s strongest non-model-specific developer/design tools, with recent updates on September 27.

sections.title: jaredpalmer/kev
sections.description: A family of trainable, locally runnable Jev-like decision models built on Qwen models.
sections.content: A family of trainable, locally runnable Jev-like decision models built on Qwen models. It shows the typed-decision idea extending into alternative open model implementations; it was updated on September 29.

sections.title: tamaratran/fast-jev-compaction
sections.description: A Claude Code plugin that uses Jev decisions to select or trim stale tool context while preserving retained content.
sections.content: A Claude Code plugin that uses Jev decisions to select or trim stale tool context while preserving retained content. It applies the decision-model approach to a concrete coding-agent bottleneck: context compaction.

sections.title: zai-org/ZCode
sections.content: Z.ai’s extensible coding-agent harness. It is a high-profile new entrant in the coding-agent harness space, with pushes through September 29.

sections.title: jev-chat/jev-chat-jarvis
sections.description: An Android conversation assistant that reads on-screen chats and offers suggested replies for the user to insert.
sections.content: An Android conversation assistant that reads on-screen chats and offers suggested replies for the user to insert. It demonstrates the Jev/typed-decision wave moving from developer workflows into a mobile assistant use case.

sections.title: mizorewww/laya-mlx
sections.description: A native Apple MLX runtime for Laya decision models, targeting local low-latency inference.
sections.content: A native Apple MLX runtime for Laya decision models, targeting local low-latency inference. It adds an Apple Silicon/local-inference deployment path to the Laya ecosystem.

sections.title: robbietilton/Compositor
sections.description: A native macOS image editor positioned as a Photoshop alternative.
sections.content: A native macOS image editor positioned as a Photoshop alternative. It is a standout consumer desktop application among the month’s otherwise AI-heavy breakouts.

sections.title: Mak5er/AirCard
sections.description: An iOS utility for customizing Apple Wallet card appearances without a jailbreak.
sections.content: An iOS utility for customizing Apple Wallet card appearances without a jailbreak. It is another unusually popular native Apple-platform utility created in September.

sections.title: Albert-Weasker/niubigeo
sections.description: An open-source tool for AI brand-visibility and competitor reporting.
sections.content: An open-source tool for AI brand-visibility and competitor reporting. It reflects demand for practical AI-search visibility and marketing analytics tools, beyond model and agent infrastructure.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content: Typed decisions and the Laya/Jev ecosystem span model checkpoints, local inference, coding-agent context management, and mobile assistance (Laya, kev, fast-jev-compaction, jev-chat-jarvis, laya-mlx). Coding-agent and harness activity is represented by jev-ultrafast and ZCode. m3e-canvas and niubigeo show AI-assisted design and AI-search marketing applications. HowToLiveBetter, Compositor, and AirCard show substantial attention beyond AI infrastructure. In this selected set: Python 4 repositories; TypeScript 4; Swift 2; HTML 1; Kotlin 1.

sections.title: Notable Shifts
sections.content: The sharpest pattern is the quick translation of a new decision-model idea into surrounding products: local runtimes, coding-agent plugins, web agents, and mobile assistants. At the same time, attention is not exclusively going to AI infrastructure: a Chinese-language life guide and native Mac/iOS utilities appear among the month’s most-starred new repositories.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: September’s repository-level momentum points to developer interest in smaller, typed decisions as a complement to full text generation, especially where latency and context costs matter. The ecosystem is still early, and current star totals do not establish adoption or quality; the cross-project spread is the signal to watch. Practical knowledge repositories and native desktop/mobile utilities also remain capable of breaking through.

method_note: GitHub Search and REST repository metadata were used. Monthly star deltas are unavailable from these endpoints; stars_gained is null. Rankings use current star totals among repositories created during September and recent push dates for freshness, with duplicates/list-style noise filtered where identified.
